summary: SLA dependency-graph inconsistency causes stale SLA inheritance after template rename
description: Issue summary: After several template renames and bulk imports last week, the SLA dependency graph that derives effective SLA weights for autoroute macros is returning stale parent bindings for a subset of templates. Impact: internal routing is mis-prioritizing support queues for about ~2.3% of incoming internal tickets causing delayed escalations and inaccurate SLA reporting buckets in the ops dashboard. Scope: internal-support only; no customer-facing queues affected, but impacts internal on-call SLO reporting and automated escalations. Hypothesis: when template_registry entries are renamed or re-keyed, the dependency graph reconciliation job sometimes fails to update in-memory binding indices, leaving older template IDs referenced by compiled macros. This yields an effective SLA weight mismatch between computed routing decisions and the persisted template manifest.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a template 'HighTouch-DB-Migrations-v1' with SLA weight = P0 (10) and bind to macro 'db-migration-alerts'

2) Bulk-rename template to 'HighTouch-DB-Migrations-archived' via template-import job (template_registry import v2) and create new template 'HighTouch-DB-Migrations' with a different ID and SLA weight = P2 (3)
3) Trigger reconcile-run (manual run of sla-dependency-reconciler) but observe logs: job reports 'partial-sync: 37/49 reconciled' without error code
4) Send a test internal ticket matching macro 'db-migration-alerts' and observe routing: ticket routed with previous P0 priority instead of the new P2 weight
5) Check in-memory dependency graph endpoint /internal/debug/dep-graph?macro=db-migration-alerts and note parent template ID still points to the archived template ID
6) Query DB: SELECT * FROM template_bindings WHERE macro='db-migration-alerts' shows both bindings present; reconcile job should have pruned the archived binding but did not.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 - Initial triage by Maya: reproduced locally using staging copy of template_registry; confirmed reconcile reports partial-sync without throwing exception; suspect batching window in reconcile job is skipping orphaned bindings when import metadata contains 'rename' marker.

2026-03-11 - Ethan injected additional logging into sla-reconciler: discovered a race where template-imports create a tombstone + new template in same transaction; reconciler iterate over listing but uses cached index that is lazily refreshed every 60s, causing missed pruning of tombstones.

2026-03-12 - SRE (Priya Kapoor) reviewed memory cache TTL; found cache.default_ttl is 60s and reconcile batching sets page_size=200. When import volume spikes, last page is skipped by condition 'if page_count == 0 break' which is off-by-one in current implementation.

Observed side-effect: reporting pipelines compute SLA cohorts from the in-memory dep-graph endpoint; since it retained archived binding, historical daily reports for 2026-03-09 show an inflated P0 count for internal queues.
Temporary mitigation tested: manual run of 'sla-dependency-reconciler --force-full-sync' cleared stale bindings and subsequent routing adhered to updated weights.
customer_impact: internal teams only — delayed escalations for internal-support tickets and incorrect SLA cohort counts in ops dashboards. No external customer SLOs impacted.
diagnostic_commands: psql -c "SELECT macro, template_id, binding_state FROM template_bindings WHERE macro='db-migration-alerts'" support_metadata_db
kubectl logs -n infra deployment/sla-reconciler --since=2h | grep partial-sync
short_term_workaround: Run 'sla-dependency-reconciler --force-full-sync' on prod in maintenance window (low traffic). If immediate routing correctness is required, manually update macro binding to point to new template ID via admin console (not recommended at scale).
long_term_fix_candidates: 1) Fix reconciler pagination off-by-one and add deterministic watermark to detect missed pages
2) Reduce cache.default_ttl to 5s during import windows or add cache invalidation hook from template-import job
3) Add end-to-end test that simulates rename+import and asserts reconciler prunes tombstones
4) Emit reconciliation metrics (pages_scanned, pages_skipped) and alert on partial-sync rates > 0 for > 10 minutes
